name: REGRESSION PROOF — after slice 2 builds, slice 1's accepted functionality still works when the code is EXECUTED; the same probe DETECTS the loss when the scope is shrunk (PHASE-56 W-2, R-20)
description: PHASE-56 W-2, ruling R-20: the invariant must be exercised, not merely asserted. Both legs run the REAL materializerEngine and then EXECUTE the generated program with node through the L2 shell.run_in_workspace tool, reading real stdout — no forced verdict. STATED PLAINLY: this does NOT use builtproject.run_scenarios, because that harness's only setup action is start_server and it always polls a port, which would add the known port-bound flake class (PHASE-24 backlog) to the suite; executing the generated program directly is a stronger exercise and adds none. The causal link is real: a prompt-conditioned codegen stub emits an implementation containing exactly the features whose acceptance-criterion ids appear in the scoped spec it is given, so the SCOPE determines the CODE. GUARDED leg: slice 2's cumulative scope regenerates the workspace and running it prints CREATE_OK, LIST_OK (slice 1's accepted criteria) and DELETE_OK (slice 2's) — slice 1 survived the rebuild. CONTROL leg: the same stub fed a SHRUNKEN slice-2-only scoped spec (the pre-invariant behaviour, reached by calling scopedSpec directly and bypassing the production guard) regenerates a program that no longer prints CREATE_OK or LIST_OK — the exact silent deletion F-4 predicted. The control is what makes the guarded leg meaningful: it proves the probe can see the defect the invariant prevents.
